---
title: "How far should I move the ballast?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

What moving the fitted coin can and cannot achieve, and what it takes to put the
balance point back where the design wants it.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Specified
**As built: 16 g, balance point 164.0 mm aft of the nose, 1p coin centred at
24 mm** · measured on the built glider by the user, 2026-08-30.

**Fix chosen: replace the 1p with a 2p** · decided by the user, 2026-08-31 · one
coin rather than two, and it lands on the flat of the fuselage ahead of the wing.
:::

```{python}
M, XCG = 0.016, 0.1640                     # as built
PENNY, PENNY_X, PENNY_D = 3.56e-3, 0.0240, 20.3e-3
TWOPENCE, TWOPENCE_D = 7.12e-3, 25.9e-3

x_target = neutral_point() - 0.10 * c_w    # the specified 10% MAC
need = XCG - x_target

# Moving a fixed mass: the CG shifts by m*travel/M, so invert for the travel.
travel = need * M / PENNY
x_nose = PENNY_D / 2                       # coin edge just touching the nose tip
best_by_moving = XCG - PENNY * (PENNY_X - x_nose) / M

# Swapping it: solve for where the heavier coin must sit.
x_2p = (x_target * (M - PENNY + TWOPENCE) - (M * XCG - PENNY * PENNY_X)) / TWOPENCE
M_2p = M - PENNY + TWOPENCE

options = {
    "as built, 1p at 24 mm": (M, XCG),
    "1p pushed against the nose": (M, best_by_moving),
    "2p at its solved station": (M_2p, x_target),
    "the design, for reference": (0.01550, x_target),
}
flown = {}
for k, (m, x) in options.items():
    t = trim(m, x)
    flown[k] = (t, *stall(t["V"]))
```

**Answer.** You cannot fix it by moving that coin. Shifting the balance the
`{python} f"{need*1e3:.1f}"` mm it needs would take
`{python} f"{travel*1e3:.0f}"` mm of travel from a
`{python} f"{PENNY*1e3:.2f}"` g coin in a `{python} f"{M*1e3:.0f}"` g aeroplane,
which puts it `{python} f"{abs(PENNY_X - travel)*1e3:.0f}"` mm *ahead of the
nose*. Pushed as far forward as it physically goes — centred
`{python} f"{x_nose*1e3:.1f}"` mm back, its edge on the tip — it buys
`{python} f"{(XCG - best_by_moving)*1e3:.1f}"` mm of the
`{python} f"{need*1e3:.1f}"` mm required, leaving the glider trimmed level with
its stall instead of past it. Better, still not flying.

The fix is more ballast, not relocated ballast. **Replace the 1p with a 2p,
centred `{python} f"{x_2p*1e3:.0f}"` mm from the nose.** That brings the glider
to `{python} f"{M_2p*1e3:.2f}"` g balancing at
`{python} f"{x_target*1e3:.1f}"` mm, trimming
`{python} f"{flown['2p at its solved station'][1] - flown['2p at its solved station'][0]['alpha']:.1f}"`°
below the stall rather than above it, and gliding
`{python} f"{flown['2p at its solved station'][0]['LD']*1.5:.1f}"` m from 1.5 m.

That is marginally *further* than the `{python} f"{0.01550*1e3:.2f}"` g design
manages, which is worth a second look before it is mistaken for a free lunch.
The extra weight raises the trim speed from
`{python} f"{flown['the design, for reference'][0]['V']:.2f}"` to
`{python} f"{flown['2p at its solved station'][0]['V']:.2f}"` m/s, and at the
higher Reynolds number the section does slightly better — enough to offset the
mass. It buys distance by flying faster, not by flying better: sink rate rises
from `{python} f"{flown['the design, for reference'][0]['sink']:.2f}"` to
`{python} f"{flown['2p at its solved station'][0]['sink']:.2f}"` m/s, so it is
airborne for less time.

A `{python} f"{TWOPENCE_D*1e3:.1f}"` mm coin at that station sits on the flat of
the fuselage well ahead of the wing, and placement is forgiving: a millimetre
either way is worth about
`{python} f"{TWOPENCE/M_2p*1e3/c_w*1e-3*100*1e3:.2f}"`% of MAC.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-options
#| tbl-cap: "Each option at its own trim, with the stall angle from the corrected first-peak search."
import pandas as pd

pd.DataFrame({
    "": list(options),
    "mass [g]": [f"{options[k][0]*1e3:.2f}" for k in options],
    "balance [mm]": [f"{options[k][1]*1e3:.1f}" for k in options],
    "trims at": [f"{flown[k][0]['alpha']:.1f}°" for k in options],
    "stall": [f"{flown[k][1]:.1f}°" for k in options],
    "margin": [f"{flown[k][1] - flown[k][0]['alpha']:+.1f}°" for k in options],
    "range [m]": [f"{flown[k][0]['LD']*1.5:.1f}" for k in options],
}).style.hide(axis="index")
```
